steps.intent: Our objective is to secure a humanitarian pause leading to a cessation of hostilities, protect Palestinian civilians, secure hostage release, and keep the Security Council focused on a two-State horizon without explicitly endorsing Israel’s military operation. The main difficulty is satisfying the United States and United Kingdom: any immediate ceasefire language risks a veto, while co-sponsors Sudan and Venezuela will press for stronger condemnation of Israel. We therefore retained generic condemnation of terrorism and self-defence language while preserving a cessation-of-hostilities horizon and robust humanitarian and accountability provisions.

messages.Albania: Albania welcomes the inclusion of the right to self-defence and the demand for the release of all hostages, but the text still fails to identify Hamas and its 7 October terrorist attacks. We cannot support a resolution that does not condemn Hamas explicitly and unequivocally. We therefore request the operative condemnation in OP2 and the preambular reference in PP4, as well as an explicit reference to Israel’s right to self-defence in PP6.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the humanitarian objectives of the draft and welcomes its reaffirmation of self-defence and the two-State solution. To make the text balanced and viable, we ask the penholder to add an explicit condemnation of the Hamas terrorist attacks of 7 October and to strengthen OP1 with a clear call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. Brazil is ready to work constructively to avoid another veto.
messages.China: China thanks the Russian Federation for its draft and supports it as a basis for the Council’s action. To reflect the Council’s responsibilities and the international consensus, China requests that OP1 clearly call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and an end to hostilities, that OP4 call for lifting the blockade and closure of Gaza, and that OP9 explicitly reaffirm the end of the occupation and realization of the independent State of Palestine. These changes are essential; with them China can support the text.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador welcomes the improvements on humanitarian access, protection of civilians and hostages, but the text still lacks the explicit condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks that Ecuador has consistently demanded. We also ask that the Council call clearly for rescission of the evacuation order in northern Gaza and for safe return of displaced civilians. With these changes Ecuador can support the draft.
messages.France: France supports the Council's urgent responsibility on humanitarian access, protection of civilians, release of hostages and the two-State solution. But the text cannot be supported without an explicit condemnation of the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas that began on 7 October and a clear recall of Israel's right to self-defence alongside international humanitarian law. We ask the penholder to incorporate these amendments so that France can vote in favour.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the draft’s humanitarian focus and will work to strengthen it. We need an explicit immediate humanitarian ceasefire and a clear condemnation of the 7 October attacks and all terrorism, alongside unconditional hostage release and unhindered humanitarian access. We also seek clear language against forced displacement and support for regional diplomatic efforts. These changes would make the text more balanced and implementable.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports this draft as a basis for Council action and welcomes its humanitarian and two-State elements. To preserve the broadest possible agreement, we request an explicit condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas and hostage-taking; with that balance, Ghana can support the text. We also urge the penholder to reflect the Secretary-General's call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in OP1.
messages.Japan: Japan appreciates the humanitarian focus of the draft and supports its calls for humanitarian pauses, protection of civilians, access, and release of hostages. However, Japan cannot join consensus without an explicit condemnation of the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups against Israel that began on 7 October 2023. We urge the penholder to reflect this in the text and to allow sufficient time for broad consultations so that the Council can speak with one voice.
messages.Malta: Malta welcomes the improved balance of the revised text and can support it with targeted amendments. We ask the penholder to include an explicit condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks of 7 October and Israel's right to self-defence within international law, and to strengthen the demand for the safe and unconditional release of all hostages. We would also prefer OP1 to stress immediacy and OP4 to cover all available crossings under UN coordination and deconfliction.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique welcomes the Russian Federation's text and will support it, as it did earlier humanitarian drafts, because it addresses the catastrophic situation in Gaza and the protection of civilians. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP1 with an explicit call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, and to make OP4 and OP6 more operational by requiring unconditional access through all crossings, including fuel, and by rejecting any forced displacement or evacuation order. These changes are consistent with international humanitarian law and Mozambique's call for a political solution based on the two-State vision.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland welcomes the draft's humanitarian focus and its insistence on humanitarian access, protection of civilians and the release of hostages. However, Switzerland cannot support a text that does not explicitly condemn the terrorist attacks carried out by Hamas on 7 October 2023 and the taking of hostages. We also ask that the text expressly provide the ICRC with access to all hostages, ensure humanitarian access through all crossing points without conditions, and affirm the right of displaced civilians to return voluntarily and safely. We are ready to work constructively to reach a text that the Council can support.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the draft's humanitarian focus and will work to strengthen it. Our central ask is an explicit reference to an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, not only pauses, and a call to rescind the evacuation order for northern Gaza. We also seek operational language on all crossings, fuel and medical supplies to hospitals and UNRWA shelters, and an independent investigation into the Al-Ahli Hospital attack. We are ready to engage constructively.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the draft's recognition of the right to self-defence and the need for humanitarian pauses and access, but it cannot support a text that fails to name Hamas's terrorist attacks of 7 October. We ask the penholder to add an express condemnation of Hamas and hostage-taking, a clear reference to Israel's right to self-defence under the Charter, and language on Hamas's use of civilians as human shields. With those changes, the United Kingdom could support the text.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this text as drafted. It must explicitly condemn Hamas's terrorist attacks, affirm Israel's inherent right to self-defence under Article 51, and ensure that any pauses are humanitarian rather than a ceasefire. Without these changes, we will oppose the resolution.

steps.summary: The revised text balances an explicit condemnation of Hamas and Israel's right to self-defence with strengthened humanitarian access, protection and political language. It avoids an operative ceasefire call, leading several members who sought one to abstain, but it is expected to secure sufficient support without a permanent-member veto.

messages.Albania: Albania welcomes the incorporation of the condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks and of Israel's right to self-defence, which were essential for us. We remain concerned that OP6 prejudges Israel's measures to protect civilians and that OP10 moves beyond the humanitarian focus into final-status issues. With those adjustments, Albania is prepared to support the text.
messages.Brazil: Brazil welcomes the incorporation of the condemnation of Hamas's 7 October attacks and the strengthened humanitarian access provisions. We can support the text if OP1 keeps the immediate humanitarian ceasefire as the objective while retaining pauses as an interim measure, and if OP2 explicitly includes Palestinian civilians in Gaza among those protected from violence. This balanced language is essential for Brazil's position.
messages.China: China appreciates the incorporation of stronger language in OP4 and OP9 and remains ready to support Council action. However, the core gap is OP1: the text still only calls for pauses and expressly excludes a ceasefire, which cannot meet the gravity of the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. China therefore requests an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and end to hostilities in OP1, with the contradictory 'does not constitute a ceasefire' language removed, and asks that collective punishment of civilians be explicitly rejected.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador welcomes the penholder’s incorporation of our earlier requests, including the clear condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks and the call to rescind the evacuation order for northern Gaza. The revised text reflects a balanced and negotiated basis for Council action and contains the essential humanitarian, protection and accountability elements Ecuador has consistently supported. We therefore support the current draft and urge all members to unite behind it and ensure its full and immediate implementation, including humanitarian access, the release of all hostages and respect for international humanitarian law.
messages.France: France welcomes the revisions, which incorporate our key requests: the strongest condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks and explicit recognition of Israel’s right to self-defence. The text now provides a balanced basis for the Council to address the humanitarian emergency while upholding international humanitarian law. France supports the current text and will vote in favour; we urge all members to unite behind it.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the inclusion of the condemnation of the 7 October attacks, the rejection of forced displacement and the call for renewed diplomacy. However, given the total collapse of health services and the extreme humanitarian emergency in Gaza, Gabon cannot support a text that still stops short of calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We therefore maintain our red line on OP1: the Council must call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, with humanitarian pauses and corridors as part of its implementation, not as a substitute for it.
messages.Ghana: Ghana welcomes the revision, particularly the strong condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas and the focus on humanitarian access. We support the text as a basis for Council action, but we continue to believe OP1 should signal a political horizon beyond temporary pauses. We therefore ask the penholder to add language that these humanitarian pauses should lead to a sustainable cessation of hostilities, consistent with the Council's responsibility to de-escalate the conflict.
messages.Japan: Japan welcomes the inclusion of an unequivocal condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks and hostage-taking, which was our red line. We can support the text if OP10 is aligned with resolution 2334 (2016) and leaves final status issues, including Jerusalem, to negotiations, and if the diplomatic efforts of the United States are explicitly acknowledged alongside Egypt, Qatar and the United Nations. Japan remains committed to a united Council text that delivers humanitarian relief and supports de-escalation.
messages.Malta: Malta welcomes the incorporation of its previous requests, in particular the clear condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas, the reaffirmation of Israel's right to self-defence in accordance with international law, the demand for the immediate, safe and unconditional release of all hostages with ICRC access, and the provisions on crossings and humanitarian notification. The revised text is balanced and humanitarian in focus. Malta supports the current draft as it stands and urges the Council to adopt it without further amendment so that it can be implemented without delay.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique welcomes the inclusion of unconditional humanitarian access, fuel delivery and protections against forced displacement, and can support the text. We continue to believe that the Council must call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, as the Secretary-General has urged, because humanitarian pauses alone cannot meet the scale of the crisis. We ask the penholder to add a new operative paragraph to this effect; Mozambique will support the resolution with that addition.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks the penholder for incorporating its key requests, in particular the explicit condemnation of Hamas’s attacks and hostage-taking, ICRC access, all crossings and voluntary return. The revised text now meets Switzerland’s humanitarian, protection and two-State priorities and maintains a balanced framework. Switzerland can support the text as it stands and urges the Council to act in unity.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE welcomes the incorporation of the rescission of the evacuation order, sustained humanitarian access and the Al-Ahli investigation. However, the current text still fails to meet the Council's responsibility to stop the bloodshed: it calls only for pauses and explicitly excludes a ceasefire. We cannot support this text unless OP1 is revised to call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and to demand that all parties cease hostilities; humanitarian pauses must supplement, not replace, a ceasefire.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the inclusion of our red lines on condemning Hamas, Israel's Article 51 right of self-defence, and Hamas's use of human shields. To support this text, we need OP6 amended so that it does not call for rescission of Israel's evacuation order but instead requires safe, voluntary and temporary movement with return as soon as conditions permit. We also ask that OP8 not single out Al-Ahli hospital in a way that prejudges responsibility, and that OP10 avoid pre-empting final status negotiations on Jerusalem.
messages.United States of America: We appreciate the penholder's incorporation of our redlines on condemning Hamas and affirming Israel's right of self-defence. However, we cannot support the text as drafted because it still calls for a cessation of hostilities, demands rescission of Israel's evacuation order, and prejudges Jerusalem's final status. We ask for the changes above to align the text with the principle that humanitarian pauses are not a ceasefire and that final status issues must be negotiated.

steps.summary: The revised text shifts OP1 to an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and end to hostilities while retaining strong condemnation of Hamas, humanitarian access, and balanced two-State language. Russia, China, UAE, Gabon, Brazil, Mozambique and Ghana are expected to vote in favour, while the United States and United Kingdom vote against and six others abstain. The US negative vote constitutes a veto, so the draft is not adopted.

vetoed_by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

reasons.Albania: Albania's important amendments on OP6 and OP10 were rejected, leaving language it considers unbalanced and prejudicial to final-status negotiations. Abstention aligns with its prior pattern of abstaining on Russian drafts while supporting balanced humanitarian texts.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil supported the draft after its key priorities—an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and explicit reference to Palestinian civilians—were incorporated. Its long-standing position favouring humanitarian action, protection of civilians, condemnation of terrorism and the two-State solution supports a yes vote.
reasons.China: China’s requested changes on an immediate ceasefire and on collective punishment were accepted, aligning the text with its established position; consistent with its prior votes on ceasefire and humanitarian drafts, China supports the resolution.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador had already indicated support in the last negotiation round and no outstanding requests; the Russian draft contains Ecuador’s key priorities, including condemnation of Hamas, humanitarian access, hostage release, and respect for international humanitarian law. Speaking before the vote allows Ecuador to explain its support for a text it believes can help stop civilian suffering while reaffirming a two-State horizon.
reasons.France: France's last negotiation position was support, and the draft aligns with its calls for a humanitarian ceasefire, condemnation of Hamas, protection of civilians, and release of hostages. France would vote in favour and is unlikely to speak before the vote.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon has consistently supported humanitarian ceasefire drafts and its red-line request on OP1 was accepted; it is likely to vote in favour. It generally explains its vote after the vote rather than before, so no pre-vote statement is needed.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana historically abstained on the 25 October Russian draft. Its important requested change was only partially accepted, and Ghana generally avoids endorsing polarizing texts that do not fully reflect a balanced, consensus-oriented approach.
reasons.Japan: Japan’s important requests were only partially accepted and its request to explicitly welcome US diplomatic efforts was rejected; Japan has consistently abstained on Russian drafts in this crisis while stressing balance and US-led diplomacy. Abstention is therefore the most consistent choice.
reasons.Malta: Malta had supported the balanced Brazilian text and earlier abstained on Russian drafts lacking essential elements; this text incorporates condemnation of Hamas, hostages, humanitarian access, self-defence and two-State language, matching Malta's stated red lines. Therefore Malta votes in favour and explains its vote before the vote.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique has consistently supported ceasefire and humanitarian access drafts, and its requested immediate humanitarian ceasefire was integrated into OP1. The text aligns with its calls for civilian protection, humanitarian access and a two-State solution.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia authored the draft and would vote in favour as it advances its position on an immediate ceasefire and humanitarian access while also condemning Hamas attacks. Speaking before the vote allows Russia to press for Council unity and blame obstruction on others.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland’s last negotiation position was clear support with no requested changes, and the text matches its priorities of humanitarian ceasefire, protection of civilians, hostage release, and unhindered aid access. Consistent with its established practice in these debates, it would not take the floor before the vote.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE has consistently backed ceasefire resolutions, including prior Russian drafts, and the final text includes an immediate humanitarian ceasefire alongside condemnation of Hamas and provisions on humanitarian access and forced displacement, satisfying its red line. As a strong advocate for ending the violence and assisting Gaza’s civilians, UAE would vote in favour.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK’s red-line request on OP6 was not met, and the draft’s immediate humanitarian ceasefire language conflicts with the UK position favouring pauses tied to Israel’s right to self-defence. The UK would therefore vote against alongside the United States.
reasons.United States of America: The U.S. at this date opposed an immediate ceasefire, insisted on humanitarian pauses, and treated the rescission and ceasefire provisions as red lines; those were not accepted, so the U.S. would veto.

before.Albania: Albania will abstain in the vote on this draft resolution. We strongly condemn the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October and demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We also support urgent humanitarian access and efforts to alleviate the catastrophic situation in Gaza. However, the text before us still contains unbalanced provisions and language that prejudges final status issues and does not fully reflect the core concerns we raised during the negotiations. A credible Council response must unequivocally condemn terrorism, recognize Israel's right to self-defence, protect civilians, and facilitate humanitarian pauses without prejudging the outcome of negotiations. That is why we will abstain.
before.Brazil: Brazil will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We do so because it responds to the most urgent imperative before the Council: an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Brazil unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October and all violence against civilians, including Palestinian civilians in Gaza. We stress that all parties must respect international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands that this Council act without further delay. Brazil also reiterates its commitment to a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace within secure and recognised borders, in accordance with international law and relevant resolutions, including resolution 2334 (2016).
before.China: China will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The situation in Gaza is extremely grave, and the Security Council must not remain silent. An immediate humanitarian ceasefire and an end to hostilities are the most urgent task. We welcome the incorporation of the call for extended humanitarian pauses and humanitarian corridors, the rejection of collective punishment, and the demand for safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access. China urges all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, release all hostages, and comply with international humanitarian law. We support the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. We hope the Council will send a clear and unified signal to de-escalate the situation and ease the humanitarian catastrophe.
before.Ecuador: Ecuador votes in favour of this draft resolution. We have consistently stated that the Security Council cannot remain silent while civilians suffer and international peace and security are threatened. The text before us includes essential elements that my delegation has supported: the unequivocal condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October, the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and humanitarian pauses, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians, medical personnel, hospitals and United Nations facilities. It also reaffirms the obligation of all parties to respect international humanitarian law and the need for a political horizon based on the two-State solution and resolution 2334 (2016). Ecuador remains deeply concerned by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, and we call on all parties to implement this resolution in good faith so that relief can reach those in need, hostages can return to their families, and the path towards a just and lasting peace can be restored.
before.Ghana: Ghana thanks the sponsors for their efforts to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. We support the urgent need for humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, the release of all hostages and a sustainable cessation of hostilities, and we remain committed to a two-State solution. However, Ghana had sought an explicit operative reaffirmation that the measures called for in this draft are without prejudice to the inherent right of self-defence under the Charter and in full conformity with international humanitarian law. That requested balance has been only partially reflected. In the interest of Council unity and a balanced text that can secure the broadest possible support, Ghana will abstain on this draft resolution.
before.Japan: Japan thanks the Russian Federation for its efforts. Japan unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other groups on 7 October, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and calls for rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to civilians in Gaza. Given the catastrophic humanitarian situation, the Security Council must act with unity and balance. Japan engaged constructively and requested changes to ensure the text reflects the diplomatic efforts of the United States and others and a balanced approach to final status issues. While some of our concerns were addressed, others were not, and the overall balance remains insufficient. Japan will therefore abstain.
before.Malta: Malta will vote in favour of the draft resolution before us. We do so because the text now reflects the essential elements that the Council must address: the unequivocal condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas against Israel on 7 October, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the imperative of safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access to the people of Gaza, including fuel, food, water and medical supplies. Malta supports the call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and extended humanitarian pauses, and stresses that all parties must comply with international humanitarian law and the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution. We reiterate Israel’s right to self-defence, which must be exercised in accordance with international law. The draft also rightly rejects forced displacement and reaffirms the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and call on all parties to de-escalate and protect civilians.
before.Mozambique: Mozambique will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because the Council must not remain silent in the face of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the continuing loss of civilian life. We welcome the inclusion of an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and a clear call for full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need, including fuel, food, water, medical supplies and electricity. We also stress the obligation of all parties to respect international humanitarian law, to protect civilians, medical personnel, hospitals, humanitarian workers and civilian infrastructure, and to release all hostages immediately and unconditionally. Mozambique reiterates that the suffering of civilians must end, and that the only sustainable path remains a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution, in accordance with relevant United Nations resolutions, including resolution 2334 (2016). The Security Council must act with urgency and unity; the people of Gaza and Israel need it to act now.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of this draft resolution. It responds to the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, demands an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and unhindered humanitarian access, condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas and all violence against civilians, and calls for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. It also rightly rejects any forced displacement of the Palestinian civilian population and reaffirms the need for a political settlement based on the two-State solution and the relevant Security Council resolutions. We call upon all members of the Council to support this balanced text. The Council cannot remain passive while civilians are dying, hospitals are collapsing and humanitarian supplies are blocked. Attempts to dilute or delay the Council’s response are unacceptable. We urge the Council to assume its responsibility and adopt this resolution without further obstruction.
before.United Arab Emirates: Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates will vote in favour of this draft. The situation in Gaza is catastrophic: civilians have nowhere safe to go, hospitals are collapsing, and humanitarian access remains grossly insufficient. We support this text because it demands an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, safe and unhindered delivery of aid, protection of civilians and medical facilities, and the rescission of orders that could amount to forcible displacement. We unequivocally condemn the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October and all attacks against civilians. The Council must act now to save lives and uphold international humanitarian law. We call on all members to unite behind a humanitarian ceasefire and a political horizon based on the two-State solution.
before.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States remains intensively engaged in diplomacy to secure the release of hostages, prevent a wider conflict, protect civilians, and deliver lifesaving humanitarian assistance to Gaza. We unequivocally condemn Hamas’s terrorist attacks, and we continue to affirm Israel’s inherent right to self-defence. We support humanitarian pauses and corridors so that aid can reach Palestinians in need. But the United States cannot support this draft. It calls for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and an end to hostilities, which would leave Hamas in place and able to repeat the atrocities of 7 October. It also demands the rescission of Israel’s evacuation warning and contains other unbalanced provisions that would constrain Israel’s ability to defend itself while Hamas continues to hold hostages and fire indiscriminately at Israeli civilians. The Council must act in a way that advances real diplomacy and reflects the facts on the ground. For these reasons, the United States cannot support this resolution and will vote against it.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution. We deeply regret that the Security Council has once again failed to adopt a text calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, an end to hostilities, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and the release of all hostages. The result does not change the fact that the situation in Gaza is catastrophic and that the Council must not remain silent.

China condemns all acts that harm civilians and all violations of international humanitarian law. We unequivocally condemn the terrorist attacks by Hamas against Israel on 7 October, demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and call for the protection of civilians, hospitals, medical personnel, humanitarian workers and United Nations personnel. At the same time, the indiscriminate suffering of Palestinian civilians, the collapse of health services, the denial of adequate humanitarian supplies and any forced displacement are unacceptable and must stop.

The immediate priority is to bring about a humanitarian ceasefire, de-escalate the situation, open and sustain humanitarian corridors, and ensure rapid, safe and unhindered relief to all civilians in need. Military means cannot solve this crisis. The two-State solution based on the 1967 lines and the relevant United Nations resolutions remains the only viable path to lasting peace.

China calls on the Security Council to shoulder its responsibilities, put aside geopolitical calculations and send a clear, unified signal for peace. We will continue to work with all parties to ease the humanitarian catastrophe and promote a comprehensive, just and lasting settlement of the Palestinian question.
after.Ecuador: Mr. President, Ecuador voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that the Council has once again been unable to adopt it owing to the negative votes of permanent members. We have already explained our position, but we wish to reiterate that the Security Council cannot remain silent while civilians in Gaza face a catastrophic humanitarian situation and while international peace and security are threatened. The text contained essential elements: condemnation of the Hamas terrorist attacks of 7 October, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and humanitarian pauses, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and to refrain from forced displacement. Ecuador will continue to work for Council unity and for a credible political horizon based on the two-State solution. The credibility of the Council depends on its ability to act, and we will not tire in that effort.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of this draft resolution. It contained elements that France has consistently called for and that the Security Council cannot ignore: the unequivocal condemnation of the terrorist attacks committed by Hamas on 7 October, the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the call for a humanitarian ceasefire and humanitarian pauses, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to Gaza, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the rejection of any forced displacement of the Palestinian population.

France deeply regrets that the Security Council has once again been unable to adopt a resolution, despite the gravity of the situation. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza is worsening by the hour. Hospitals are collapsing, civilians lack water, food, medicine, fuel and electricity, and humanitarian workers are unable to reach those in need. The Council cannot remain silent and must assume its responsibilities.

France recalls that Israel has the right to defend itself against terrorism. But that right must be exercised in full respect of international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution. All parties must protect civilians. Hamas must immediately and unconditionally release all hostages and cease attacks against civilians. The Palestinian population of Gaza is also a victim of Hamas.

An immediate humanitarian pause is indispensable to relieve suffering and allow aid to enter. Safe, rapid and sustained humanitarian access, including through the Rafah crossing and other crossings, must be guaranteed, including fuel sufficient to restore hospitals, water and electricity. Any forced displacement of civilians is unacceptable and contrary to international law.

France will continue to work with all Council members to overcome divisions and to secure the adoption of a unified text that condemns terrorism, protects civilians, provides for humanitarian access, and preserves the political horizon. There can be no solution other than a two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security, based on the 1967 lines and the relevant Security Council resolutions. The Security Council must not resign itself to paralysis.
after.Gabon:
Mr. President,

Gabon voted in favour of this draft resolution because it responds to the most urgent imperative before the Council: an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and an end to hostilities, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to the civilian population in Gaza, the protection of civilians, medical personnel and hospitals, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and the rejection of any forced displacement of the Palestinian civilian population.

Gabon unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas against Israel on 7 October and all acts of violence against civilians. All parties must respect international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution.

We deeply regret that the Security Council has once again failed to act in the face of an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe: hospitals collapsing, shortages of fuel, food, water and medicine, and civilians paying an unbearable price. The exercise of the veto has once again prevented the Council from shouldering its responsibilities and has sent a deeply troubling message to civilians who look to us for protection and hope.

Gabon remains convinced that the Council must speak with unity and urgency. We reiterate our call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access, and de-escalation. We remain committed to a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution and on the relevant Security Council resolutions, including resolution 2334 (2016). The Council must not remain paralysed while human suffering continues to grow.
after.Malta:
Mr. President,

Malta voted in favour of the draft resolution and deeply regrets that the Council has again been unable to act in the face of a catastrophic humanitarian situation. We reiterate our unequivocal condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas against Israel on 7 October and our call for the immediate, safe and unconditional release of all hostages. We continue to recognize Israel’s right to self-defence, which must be exercised in full compliance with international humanitarian law and the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution.

The Council’s failure to adopt this text does not diminish the obligations of the parties. Civilians, hospitals, medical personnel, humanitarian workers and United Nations personnel must be protected. Safe, rapid, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access, including fuel, food, water and medical supplies, must be allowed throughout Gaza. Malta supports an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors, and rejects any forced displacement of the Palestinian civilian population. We urge all members to overcome divisions and to build on the essential elements of this draft without further delay. The Council must not remain silent while civilians continue to die. Malta remains ready to engage constructively and reiterates its commitment to a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr President,

The Russian Federation regrets that the Security Council has once again failed to act. Our draft resolution was balanced, humanitarian in substance and grounded in international law. It demanded an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. It condemned in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October, as well as all violence against civilians, including Palestinian civilians in Gaza. It rejected forced displacement and reaffirmed the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines.

The vote speaks for itself. Ten members supported the text. Only two delegations — the United States and the United Kingdom — blocked it with their vetoes. Once again, we have witnessed hypocrisy and double standards. While claiming concern for the humanitarian situation, Washington and London have prevented the Council from demanding an end to the bloodshed. They bear full responsibility for the consequences of this veto. The blood of civilians in Gaza is on their hands.

Attempts to justify this veto by references to balance are untenable. The text condemned terrorism, demanded the release of hostages and reaffirmed the right to self-defence in conformity with international law. What the vetoes have made clear is that those who blocked this resolution are not interested in saving civilian lives. They are interested in geopolitical advantage and in prolonging the conflict.

The Russian Federation will continue to insist on an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and a just political settlement on the basis of the relevant Security Council resolutions and the two-State solution. The Council must not remain silent while civilians are dying. Those who obstructed this resolution will have to answer before the international community.
after.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. The text reflected priorities that Switzerland has consistently upheld since 7 October: the unequivocal condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas and of all acts of terrorism; the immediate, safe and unconditional release of all hostages; the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure; full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access; and an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and humanitarian pauses to allow aid to reach civilians in need. It also recalled the obligation of all parties to respect international humanitarian law and reaffirmed the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines.

The humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic. Hospitals have run out of fuel, the health system has collapsed, and civilians have nowhere safe to go. Switzerland deeply regrets that this draft resolution was not adopted owing to negative votes. The Security Council must not remain paralysed while civilians continue to die and humanitarian needs continue to grow. The use of the veto must not become an excuse for inaction, and the suffering of civilians demands that this Council act with unity and urgency.

Switzerland reiterates its call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, for the protection of all civilians, including humanitarian and medical personnel and United Nations staff, and for rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Gaza. All parties must comply with international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution. Any forcible displacement of the Palestinian civilian population is unacceptable.

Switzerland remains committed to a just, lasting and comprehensive peace based on the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within recognized borders on the basis of the 1967 lines. We will continue to support the efforts of the Secretary-General and all regional and international partners to end the violence, alleviate suffering and create a political horizon.
after.United Arab Emirates: Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates voted in favour of this resolution because it contained the minimum the Council must demand: an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and medical facilities, and the rejection of forcible displacement. We deeply regret that the Council has again been unable to adopt a text that would have responded to the catastrophic situation in Gaza. Ten members supported this draft. That majority reflects the urgent demand of the international community. The Council’s failure today does not diminish the obligations of the parties under international humanitarian law, nor does it diminish our own responsibility. The humanitarian system in Gaza is collapsing. Hospitals lack fuel and medicine. Civilians have nowhere safe to go. Aid is a trickle against overwhelming need. The United Arab Emirates will continue to call for a humanitarian ceasefire, for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, for sustained and unimpeded humanitarian access, including fuel, and for the protection of civilians, hospitals, UN personnel and humanitarian workers. We reject any forced displacement of Palestinians within or outside Gaza. We reiterate that terrorism must be condemned, that all attacks against civilians are unacceptable, and that all violations must be investigated and held to account. There is no military solution. The only path is a political horizon based on the two-State solution and the relevant Security Council resolutions. The Council must not remain silent. We will continue to work with all members to achieve the unity and action that the situation demands.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President,

The United Kingdom takes the floor to explain its vote. We are appalled by Hamas’s terrorist attacks against Israel on 7 October. We unequivocally condemn those attacks, demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and affirm Israel’s inherent right to self-defence in accordance with international law. At the same time, we are deeply concerned by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. Civilians must be protected, and humanitarian access must be rapid, safe, unhindered and sustained, including food, water, fuel, medicine and electricity. The United Kingdom supports humanitarian pauses and corridors so that aid can reach those in desperate need.

For those reasons, we could not support the draft before the Council. While we welcome some improvements in the text, it called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and an end to hostilities without the conditions necessary to secure the release of hostages and to ensure that Hamas can no longer pose the threat it does to Israel. A ceasefire that leaves Hamas in place, able to rearm and repeat the atrocities of 7 October, would not bring a just or sustainable peace. The draft also contained unbalanced provisions that would constrain Israel’s legitimate right to defend itself and prejudged difficult operational questions on the ground.

The Council’s priority must be to secure the release of all hostages, to facilitate humanitarian pauses and sustained aid delivery, to protect civilians, and to prevent a wider regional escalation. The United Kingdom will continue to work with all partners towards that end and towards a political horizon based on a two-State solution. Thank you.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States has already explained its position before the vote, and I will therefore be brief. We voted against this draft because it was not balanced and would not have advanced the protection of civilians or the cause of peace. It called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and an end to hostilities while Hamas remains armed, emboldened, and able to repeat the atrocities of 7 October. It did not adequately reflect Israel’s inherent right to self-defence, and it contained provisions that would constrain Israel’s ability to defend its people and prejudged sensitive issues.

Let me be clear: the United States unequivocally condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks, including the deliberate killing and hostage-taking of civilians. We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We mourn every civilian life lost, Palestinian and Israeli, and we recognize the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. That is why we are working intensively to secure humanitarian pauses and corridors, to get fuel, food, water, and medicine to civilians, and to prevent this conflict from spreading.

The Security Council must speak and act in a way that saves lives and reinforces diplomacy, not in a way that leaves Hamas in place or undermines Israel’s right to defend itself under the Charter. The United States will continue this work with partners in the region and on this Council. We remain committed to the two-State solution and to a future in which Israelis and Palestinians can live in peace and security.
